Recent Quarterly Real GDP (Annualized)
What Is Driving Growth
Analysis

Tailwinds

Equipment Investment (+17.2%) — AI infrastructure, automation, and reshoring capex. Strongest since Q3 2023.
Government Spending (+4.4%) — Rebound after Q4 shutdown. Defense and non-defense both accelerated.
Export Surge (+13.1%) — Strong demand for U.S. services and LNG. Early-Q1 dollar weakness aided.
IP Investment (+11.6%) — Software and R&D spending elevated on generative AI buildout.

Headwinds

Import Surge (+21.1%) — Front-loaded imports ahead of tariff risks and Middle East supply disruptions (-2.67pp drag).
Residential Investment (-6.2%) — Mortgage rates (6.8%+) suppress housing. Existing home sales near decade lows.
Consumer Goods (+0.4%) — Nearly flat as consumers pull back on discretionary. Services remain the bright spot.
Inflation Persistence — PCE at 3.5%, well above 2% target. Core PCE 3.3% and rising.

Structural Forces & Disruption
SECULAR themes persist 5-10+ years regardless of the business cycle. CYCLICAL themes are tied to the current macro environment and may reverse in 1-3 years.
AI & Compute Buildout ACCELERATINGSECULAR · 5-10Y+
The scale: Hyperscaler capex hitting $725B in 2026, up 77% YoY. Amazon ($200B), Microsoft ($190B), Alphabet ($175-185B), Meta ($115-135B). [CNBC]

What it means: Massive demand for GPUs (NVDA), custom silicon (TSM, MRVL), power infrastructure, and data center REITs. AI software monetization (MSFT Copilot, GOOGL AI Overviews) in early innings. Enterprise adoption still <10% penetrated.

The risk: ROI questions are growing. $725B needs to generate returns. If AI revenue disappoints in late 2026/2027, the capex cycle could decelerate — creating a semiconductor downcycle. [FactSet]
Sector Impact Map
Semiconductors (NVDA, TSM, MRVL)Strong +
Cloud Platforms (AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL)Strong +
Power / Utilities / EnergyModerate +
Ad Tech (APP, GOOGL, META)Moderate +
Traditional IT ServicesNegative
Knowledge Work (displacement)Negative
GLP-1 & Healthcare Transformation ACCELERATINGSECULAR · 10Y+
The scale: GLP-1 market projected at $82B in 2026, growing to $150B+ by 2030. ~20M Americans now on branded GLP-1s, reaching 30M by 2030. Oral formulations launching in 2026 massively expand access. [JPMorgan] [Morgan Stanley]

The disruption: JPMorgan estimates $30-55B in annual food & beverage revenue destruction by 2030. Users consume 21% fewer calories and spend 31% less on groceries. Snack food, fast food, alcohol, and bariatric surgery all losing demand. [CNBC]

Competition: Novo Nordisk, Lilly lead, but Amgen, Viking, Roche, AstraZeneca, Pfizer all have candidates. Pricing pressure inevitable.
Sector Impact Map
GLP-1 Pharma (LLY, NVO)Strong +
Health Insurers (long term)Moderate +
Fitness / Athleisure (LULU)Mild +
Packaged Food / SnacksNegative
Fast Food / RestaurantsNegative
Alcohol / TobaccoMild -
Energy Security & Middle East Crisis ACUTE RISKCYCLICAL · 1-3Y
The crisis: Iran conflict caused the largest supply disruption in oil market history per the IEA. Strait of Hormuz restrictions affecting 27% of global crude and 20% of LNG trade. [IMF]

Macro impact: Energy prices projected +24% in 2026. Primary driver of CPI re-acceleration to 4.2%. European energy crisis 2.0 (TTF gas doubled). [World Bank]

Duration risk: Unlike 2022 (Russia-Ukraine), this affects the Hormuz choke point. Qatar LNG capacity hit — 17% reduction, 3-5 year repair. [Wikipedia]
Sector Impact Map
US LNG Exporters (LNG)Strong +
Oil Producers / E&PStrong +
Defense / Aerospace (GE, HEI, TDG)Moderate +
Airlines / TransportationStrong -
Consumer (gas prices)Negative
Deglobalization & Reshoring STRUCTURALSECULAR · 10Y+
$1.7T in reshoring announced through 2024 (+53% YoY). CHIPS Act and IRA fully operational. Semis (35%) and EV/solar (31%) dominating. Structurally inflationary as supply chains rebuild at higher cost. [Atlantic Council]
Winners:Industrials, Construction, Domestic Semis
Losers:Import-dependent retailers, Low-cost mfg
Consumer Bifurcation WORSENINGCYCLICAL · 1-3Y
K-shaped economy. Savings rate at 2.6% (crisis level). Real wages negative. Credit delinquencies rising. Sentiment near all-time lows. High-income consumers still spending; middle squeezed. [Deloitte] [CNBC]
Winners:Costco, TJX (value), Luxury, Services
Losers:Mid-tier retail, Discretionary, Housing

ME Escalation / Hormuz Closure HIGH SEVERE
Oil to $120+, deep stagflation, S&P -15-20%, flight to Treasuries. Energy stocks surge, everything else sells.
Fed Policy Error (Hike into Weakness) MED HIGH
Yield curve re-inverts, housing collapse accelerates, credit spreads blow out 200+ bps. Recession within 6-9 months.
AI Capex Disappointment MED MED
Semis correct 30-40%, Nasdaq -10-15%. Hyperscalers guide down capex. Rotation to value/defensives. NVDA, TSM, APP most exposed.
China Slowdown / Taiwan Escalation LOW SEVERE
Global semiconductor supply chain catastrophe. TSM = 90% of advanced chips. AAPL China revenue (-20% of total) at risk. Global recession scenario.
Credit Event / HY Repricing LOW MED
HY spreads from 271 to 500+ bps. Leveraged firms crushed. Small caps (-20%). Banks tighten lending. Recession risk spikes.
Inflation Expectations Unanchor MED HIGH
1Y expectations already at 4.6%. If they breach 5%, the Fed is forced into aggressive hikes regardless of growth. Replay of 2022 but from a weaker starting point.

Technology Vulnerable AI Capex +++ ROI risk SELECTIVE Macro says vulnerable (high P/E + rising rates), but AI is the largest capex cycle ever. Favor profitable AI picks (NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL). Avoid unprofitable growth.
Industrials Neutral Reshoring + Low FAVORABLE Aero aftermarket (HEI, TDG, GE) + reshoring/defense spending provide structural floor. ISM at 54 confirms expansion.
Financials Favored Alt Mgrs + Credit risk FAVORABLE Higher rates help NIM. Alt managers (APO, BX) benefit from private credit boom. Exchanges (CME, CBOE) thrive on volatility. Avoid regional banks.
Consumer Staples Favored GLP-1 risk Low SELECTIVE Defensive positioning helps macro, but GLP-1 headwind for food/beverage. Favor COST (value model) over snack/packaged food names.

Real Estate Weak Neutral Rate risk HEADWINDS Higher-for-longer rates crush cap rates and housing starts. Data center REITs are the sole bright spot (AI demand).
Utilities Favored AI Power + Low FAVORABLE Defensive in stagflation + AI data center power demand creating a structural demand surge. Best sector for dual cyclical/structural tailwind.
Materials Favored Reshoring + Cyclical NEUTRAL+ Inflation hedge + infrastructure buildout. But ISM prices surging — input costs a risk for processors. Favor commodity producers over processors.
Comm. Services Weak AI/Ads + Ad cycle SELECTIVE Worst weekly sector (-3.37%) on ad weakness. But GOOGL and NFLX have AI and subscriber tailwinds. Split within sector is wide.
Framework Summary
The cyclical regime signals caution, but structural forces add nuance. Two of the most powerful secular themes in decades — the $725B AI infrastructure buildout and the $80B+ GLP-1 revolution — are unfolding during a stagflationary macro environment. This creates conditions where sector-level dynamics may matter more than the broad market direction.

Sectors with dual tailwinds (favorable cyclical + structural positioning): Energy (inflation hedge + ME crisis), Healthcare (defensive + GLP-1), Utilities (defensive + AI power demand), and select Industrials (reshoring + aero aftermarket). See the Structural Forces tab for deeper analysis on each theme.

Tech presents a mixed signal. Cyclical indicators suggest vulnerability (elevated P/E, rising rates), but the AI capex cycle is historically unprecedented. Profitable AI infrastructure names (semis, cloud platforms) have structural support; speculative/unprofitable names carry more cyclical risk.

Key risk to monitor: Middle East escalation remains the highest-likelihood, highest-impact variable. A sustained oil spike above $120 would push the regime deeper into stagflation territory.

Factor Definitions
All scores are percentile ranks (0-100) relative to the LOGO portfolio. 50th = median. Higher = more exposure to that factor.
Momentum — 6-month price return. High = strong price trend.
Growth — Earnings + revenue growth. High = fast grower.
Value — Inverse of forward P/E. High = cheaper valuation.
Quality — Profit + operating margin. High = more profitable.
Size — Market cap. High = larger company.
Volatility — Beta. High = more volatile than market.
